Computes the mean of the squared relative differences [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the metric computes the 'mean of the squared relative differences'. However, Source [S1] defines 'SqRel' as the mean of the squared differences divided by the ground truth depth (which corresponds to the mean of squared relative differences, i.e., $E[(D_{pred} - D_{gt})^2 / D_{gt}]$). The term 'relative difference' typically implies division by the ground truth (or predicted) value, resulting in a ratio. 'Squared relative difference' would be $((D_{pred} - D_{gt}) / D_{gt})^2$. The metric 'SqRel' in the source is $((D_{pred} - D_{gt})^2) / D_{gt}$, which is the mean of squared differences weighted by the inverse of ground truth, not the mean of squared relative differences. Furthermore, the claim mentions '[S1, unofficial]', but the source does not label any metric as 'unofficial'. More critically, the mathematical definition provided in the claim ('mean of the squared relative differences') does not match the standard definition of 'SqRel' (Mean Squared Relative Error vs Mean Squared Error normalized by depth). Actually, looking closely at the formula in S1: `SqRel: |I|^-1 sum ||D_bar(p) - D_GT(p)||^2 / D_GT(p)`. This is the Mean of (Squared Difference / Ground Truth). The claim says 'mean of the squared relative differences'. A relative difference is $(D_{pred} - D_{gt})/D_{gt}$. Squared relative difference is $((D_{pred} - D_{gt})/D_{gt})^2$. The mean of this is AbsRel squared? No. The claim is mathematically ambiguous or incorrect regarding the specific metric name 'SqRel' which usually stands for 'Squared Relative Error' but is defined in the text as sum of squared errors divided by ground truth. The claim's phrasing 'squared relative differences' usually implies $((D_{pred}-D_{gt})/D_{gt})^2$, whereas the source defines SqRel as $(D_{pred}-D_{gt})^2 / D_{gt}$. These are different. Therefore, the evidence does not support the specific mathematical description in the claim for the metric named SqRel.

The square root of the mean squared error between predicted and ground truth depths [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes 'the square root of the mean squared error', which is the definition of Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). However, the provided evidence explicitly defines the RMSE metric as the square root of the mean of the squared errors divided by the ground truth depth (specifically, $|I|^{-1} p∈I ||D̄(p) − D^{GT}(p)||^2 / D^{GT}(p)$). This is a relative error metric, not the standard absolute Mean Squared Error. Furthermore, the text lists 'RMSE' and 'RMSE log' as distinct metrics, and the formula provided for RMSE includes division by $D^{GT}(p)$, making it different from the standard 'square root of the mean squared error' implied by the claim.

This factor is derived from the median ratio of ground truth to predicted depth across all images in a scene [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the factor is derived from the median ratio of ground truth to predicted depth across all images in a scene. Source [S1] explicitly defines the scene-level consistency scaling factor $s$ using the formula $s =  rac{1}{N} sum_{I_i in S} text{median}(D_i^{GT} / bar{D}_i)$. This formula calculates the median of the ratio of ground truth depth ($D_i^{GT}$) to predicted depth ($bar{D}_i$) for each image in the scene set $S$, and then averages these values. Thus, the claim accurately reflects the evidence provided.
